paite: Ka lungtang in, "Kisa in, vualnopna in ka hon entel dia; huaiziak in nopbawlna ah bual in," ngai in, hiai leng bangmah lou ahi, ka chi hi.
heading: Nopbawlna Leh Sepgimna Athawn Ahi
english: I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure;” and behold, this also was vanity.

paite: Nuihzatna thu ah, "Haina ahi," Vualnopna thu ah, "Bang ahih a?" ka chi hi.
english: I said of laughter, “It is foolishness;” and of mirth, “What does it accomplish?”

paite: Adamsung ua mite tapate'n ahih ding uh bang ahia hoih ka muh theih matan, ka lungtang in pilna kei hon pi kawm in, uain a ka sa kipahsakdan leh haina let tintendan ka lungtang in ka zong hi.
english: I searched in my heart how to cheer my flesh with wine, my heart yet guiding me with wisdom, and how to lay hold of folly, until I might see what it was good for the sons of men that they should do under heaven all the days of their lives.

paite: Nasepna thupi ka bawl a; innte ka kilam hi.
english: I made myself great works. I built myself houses. I planted myself vineyards.

paite: Grephuante ka kibawl a; huante leh gamsitte ka kibawl a, huaite ah thei chi chih ka suan hi.
english: I made myself gardens and parks, and I planted trees in them of all kinds of fruit.

paite: Gammang singte khoinate hihkawt ding in, tui lite ka kibawl hi.
english: I made myself pools of water, to water the forest where trees were grown.

paite: Pasal sikhate leh numei sikhate ka lei a, ka insung ah sikhate apiang ua; belamhon leh bawnghon ka hau a, Jerusalem a ka ma a omte tengteng sang in.
english: I bought male servants and female servants, and had servants born in my house. I also had great possessions of herds and flocks, above all who were before me in Jerusalem.

paite: Dangka leh dangka-eng leng, bialte leh kumpipate a kipan kei a ding in gou ka kaikhawm a; pasal lasa mite leh numei lasa mite, mite tapate kipahna, atam a tam meite ka nei hi.
english: I also gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces. I got myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men: musical instruments of all sorts.

paite: Huchi in Jerusalem a ka ma a om tengteng sang in ka thupi in, ka pung zaw a; ka pilna leng ka kiang ah a-om gige hi.
english: So I was great, and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also remained with me.

paite: Huan bangpeuh ka mit in alunggulh amau ka it kei hi; nopsakna himhim a kipan in ka lungtang ka len kei, ka sepgimnate tengteng ziak in ka lungtang lah akipak ngal a; huan hiai tuh ka sepgimna tengteng a kipan ka tantuan ahi.
english: Whatever my eyes desired, I didn’t keep from them. I didn’t withhold my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor, and this was my portion from all my labor.

paite: Huchi in ka khutte'n abawl uh nasep tengteng ka vel a, semgim a ka hih nasep gimna tengteng; huan, ngai in, bang teng bangmah lou leh huih nungdelh ahi a, ni nuai ah bangmah phattuamna a-om kei hi.
english: Then I looked at all the works that my hands had worked, and at the labor that I had labored to do; and behold, all was vanity and a chasing after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.

paite: Huan pilna leh lungsim kimlouhna leh haina en ding in ka kihei a; kumpipa nung a hong pai mihing in bang hihthei ding ahia? Akihih khinsa mahmah tanpha in leng.
english: I turned myself to consider wisdom, madness, and folly; for what can the king’s successor do? Just that which has been done long ago.

paite: Huchi in khovak in khomial akhen dandan in, pilna in haina kheng ahi chih ka muta hi.
english: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.

paite: Alutang ah mipil mitte a-om a, khomial ah mihai avak hi; huchi hinapi in lah thu khat mi tengteng kiang ah atung hi.
english: The wise man’s eyes are in his head, and the fool walks in darkness—and yet I perceived that one event happens to them all.

paite: Huai lai in ka lungtang in, "Mihaite kiang a ahong om bang in, huchibang in kei kiang ah leng ahong om ding; ahihleh bang ding a kei pilzaw ka hia?" ka chi hi. Huan ka lungtang in hiai mah leng bangmah lou ahi, ka chita hi.
english: Then I said in my heart, “As it happens to the fool, so will it happen even to me; and why was I then more wise?” Then I said in my heart that this also is vanity.

paite: Mipil, mihai bangmah a, theihgigena lah tangtawn in a-om ngal kei a; tunung chiang in avek ua mangngilh khit ahi ding uh chih thei in. Huan bangchi a mihai bang a mipil si ahia?
english: For of the wise man, even as of the fool, there is no memory forever, since in the days to come all will have been long forgotten. Indeed, the wise man must die just like the fool!

paite: Huchi in hinna ka hua a; ni nuai a bawl thilhih kei a ding a ahaksat ziak in; bang teng lah bangmah lou leh huih nungdelh ahi ngal a.
english: So I hated life, because the work that is worked under the sun was grievous to me; for all is vanity and a chasing after wind.

paite: Huan ni nuai a ka sepgim ka sepgimna tengteng ka hua a; ka nung a hong om ding mi kiang a ka nutsiat ngei ding ahi chih thei in.
english: I hated all my labor in which I labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.

paite: Kua'n ahia mipil hia ahihkeileh mihai ahong hih ding thei? Ka sepgimna tengteng a ka sepgimna tung ah thu anei ding a, ni nuai a pilna ka etsakna ah. Hiai leng bangmah lou ahi.
english: Who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? Yet he will have rule over all of my labor in which I have labored, and in which I have shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.

paite: Huaiziak in ni nuai a sepgimna tengteng ka na bawl tak tungtang thu a ka lungtang lungdongsak ding in ka kipumhei hi.
english: Therefore I began to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labor in which I had labored under the sun.

paite: Mi asengimna pilna leh theihna leh kivakna toh om lah a-om ngal a; himahleh huai a semgimloumi kiang ah atantuan ding a nutsiah in a-om ding hi. Hiai leng bangmah lou leh gilou lianpi ahi.
english: For there is a man whose labor is with wisdom, with knowledge, and with skillfulness; yet he shall leave it for his portion to a man who has not labored for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.

paite: Ni nuai a asepgimna tengteng a kipan leh alungtang a akisukna tengteng a kipan mihing in bang anei a le?
english: For what does a man have of all his labor and of the striving of his heart, in which he labors under the sun?

paite: Anite tengteng lungkhamna lel ahi ngal a, athuakna dahna; ahi, zan nangawn in alungtang akhawl kei hi. Hiai leng bangmah lou ahi.
english: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail is grief; yes, even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.

paite: Mihing a ding a anek a adawn a, asepgimna a thil hoih a akha abualsak val a hoihzaw bangmah a-om kei hi. Hiai leng ka thei a, Pathian khut a kipan om ahi.
english: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.

paite: Kei sang a kua'n ahia ne thei a, ahihkeileh kua'n ahia nopsakna nei zaw?
english: For who can eat, or who can have enjoyment, more than I?

paite: Amah hihlungkim mi kiang ah Pathian in pilna leh theihna leh nopsakna ape ngal a; himahleh mikhial kiang ah, gimthuakna apia, lakhawm ding leh kholkhawm ding in, huchi a kuapeuh Pathian hihlungkim kiang a apiaktheihna ding in. Hiai leng bangmah lou leh huih nungdelh lel ahi.
english: For to the man who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him who pleases God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
